_meta: A set of cache entries populated at the same moment, used to show why giving every entry the same fixed time-to-live makes them all expire together -- flooding the origin with a synchronized wave of refetches -- and why jittering each entry's TTL spreads the expirations out. A cache entry lives for its TTL and then expires, forcing a refetch from the origin on the next request. When many entries are created at once -- a cache warmed at deploy, a burst of traffic that populates the cache in one spike, a batch load -- and they all share the same TTL, they all expire at the same instant. At that instant every one of them misses simultaneously and the origin receives the whole set of refetches at once: a synchronized expiry stampede whose peak load is the number of entries, arriving in one bucket, on a backend sized for the steady trickle of refetches. The fix is to add a small random jitter to each entry's TTL so the expirations scatter across a window instead of landing together, flattening the refetch peak to roughly the number of entries divided by the window. n_entries is how many entries were populated at once; base_ttl is the shared nominal TTL; jitter_window is the number of time buckets over which jitter spreads the expirations. These are the fixture; each entry's expiry bucket under a fixed TTL and under a jittered TTL, and the peak refetches per bucket, are computed.
